about: The source files the template builders read: where each comes from, its licence and its SHA-256. The files themselves are not in this repository. A file whose checksum differs, or that is not listed, is refused unless the caller accepts it (`--accept-unlisted-sources`), and the checksum actually read is recorded in the package's origin.

fsaverage.description: FreeSurfer's fsaverage (ico7, 163842 vertices per hemisphere): the pial, white and inflated surfaces, the registered sphere (sphere.reg), and the parcellations and cortex masks named explicitly.
fsaverage.download: the `fsaverage` subject of a FreeSurfer installation (https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/)
fsaverage.licence: FreeSurfer Software License Agreement, Part B v1.0 (https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/fswiki/FreeSurferSoftwareLicense): redistribute only with the licence text and notice, keep the attributions, mark modified versions

icbm152.description: Brainstorm's default anatomy ICBM152_2026 (labelled "ICBM152 2026") (ICBM 2009c nonlinear asymmetric; FreeSurfer-derived cortex surfaces with their registered spheres): the cortex surfaces and, named explicitly, their parcellations; the MNI and SCS transforms come from subjectimage_T1.mat.
icbm152.download: the default anatomy `ICBM152` of Brainstorm (https://neuroimage.usc.edu/brainstorm/Tutorials/DefaultAnatomy); the build reads the folder it unpacks to
icbm152.licence: the MNI/ICBM152 permissive notice (license.txt in the folder: use, copy, modify and distribute for any purpose, notice kept) for the template; FreeSurfer Software License Agreement Part B v1.0 for its cortex surfaces; each parcellation under its own terms (the importer records them; a parcellation whose terms are not confirmed is not redistributable)

hcp1065.description: Whole-brain tractography on the HCP-1065 population-average diffusion template (DSI Studio), as a TrackVis .trk exported from DSI Studio; imported into the ICBM152 template package by its MNI coordinates.
hcp1065.download: DSI Studio's HCP-1065 template and tract atlas (https://brain.labsolver.org/hcp_template.html, https://brain.labsolver.org/hcp_trk_atlas.html); tracking is random, so a re-run gives other streamlines: the checksum names the realisation used
